item.title: Joe Jonas Says He Sought Therapy After His Solo Album Underperformed
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: Welcome to Trending on Billboard. Today, we're talking about Joe Jonas and his journey to finding success and mental health.
Joe Jonas recently opened up about the disappointing commercial performance of his 2011 solo debut, Fastlife. The album peaked at number 15 on the Billboard 200, and its lead single, "See No More", reached number 92 on the Hot 100. For Jonas, these results were devastating.
[Soft music plays in the background]
He shared on his podcast, Hey Jonas!, that he tied the album's outcome to his self-worth, saying, "If I do that, then I matter." As a result, he started experiencing panic attacks and physical pain. A doctor found him physically healthy but recommended therapy, which Jonas initially resisted.
[Music transitions to a more uplifting tone]
However, Jonas eventually found his way. In 2015, he formed the funk-pop band DNCE, and their debut single, "Cake by the Ocean", reached number 9 on the Billboard Hot 100. The Jonas Brothers also reunited in 2019 and topped the Billboard 200 with Happiness Begins, led by the Hot 100 number 1 single, "Sucker".
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's the story of Joe Jonas' journey to finding success and prioritizing his mental health. Thanks for tuning in to Trending on Billboard. [Outro music continues to play until the end]
